purpose: Source and navigation audit for FINDR’s selected offline keypad practice profiles. Raw research references are retained to distinguish manufacturer facts, implementation limits and fictional fixtures.

galaxy-dimension: Full-menu hierarchy 20/30/50 is retained. Direct menu numbers are contextual.
A newer/B older in the log; # gives circuit resistance and RIO voltage.
Selected walk test: # includes a zone, ent starts; no invented extra ready confirmation. All Zones means omittable zones.
Program Zones contains a zone selector, then 1 Function; full 52-value reference retained.
Already authorised session; FINDR Exit practice is separate from actual engineer logoff.
texecom-premier-elite: Numeric root choice + YES; the event-log choice digit opens directly.
Three-digit zone selection; NO edits the current Type field. No invented Zone Type submenu.
Walk test has the documented Area A choice before YES starts; Menu ends the test.
0 Log off ENGINEER + YES completes logoff with no extra confirmation. Reset stays authorised.
Type subset 0–4; other fields and diagnostic Omit/Chime are excluded. Draft cancellation is a trainer rule.
Area is implemented for walk-test views only. Additional zone/log Area views are documented in raw research but outside this version.
scantronic-ion: No verified numeric root-menu shortcuts or numeric zone-picker shortcuts.
Type shortcuts 00/03/05/06 are accepted but not displayed as type labels. The type list is explicitly a subset.
Walk Test → System starts immediately; tick finishes. Other walk-test branches are outside this version.
Left/right are contextual; neither is a global confirm/back replacement.
Accepted edits persist only on confirmed exit. v6 faults must be cleared; no later Exit with faults feature is imported.
Only All Events is implemented; later official user guide supports log controls only.
orisec-cp: Source: legacy CP-25 / CP-50 / CP-100 INS008, 2018. The catalogue family link does not expand trainer scope to CP-200.
The root screenshot and shortcut text conflict; no numeric root shortcuts are taught.
Tests & Diagnostics → Test Bell & Strobe / Walk Test Zones / View Zone Status; System Event Logs → View event log are the only implemented branches.
The documented bell/strobe controls only change fictional display state.
All populated LCD information and sample readings are simulated, using one 2k2/4k7 DEOL example.

fixturePolicy: Every populated zone, detector state, reading, event, timestamp and log category is a simulated practice fixture. Raw manuals remain the source for menu names and controls. None of the data represents a connected alarm.

galaxy.title: Galaxy Dimension
galaxy.scope: Selected full-menu workflows based on the Galaxy Dimension Installer Manual IE1-0063 Rev 1.0. This is a practice simulation, not an emulation of all firmware or hardware behaviour.

display.note: Menu names/numbers are source verified; exact LCD spacing and fixture timestamps are illustrative unless separately marked.

A.caption: A >
A.behaviour: Move forward through an option or zone list. In the event log, move forward in time to a newer event.

B.caption: < B
B.behaviour: Move backward through an option or zone list. In the event log, move backward in time to an older event.

ent.caption: ent
ent.behaviour: Open the selected option, start the selected-zone test, or save the proposed function value.

esc.caption: esc
esc.behaviour: Return one level; cancel an unsaved function edit; end a walk test.

#.behaviour: Context-specific: show zone readings, reveal log details, include/remove a selected walk-test zone, or toggle active walk-test results.

*.behaviour: Context-specific on the real panel. No function is required in the supported practice workflows. Never use as a universal back key.

digits.behaviour: Select an option valid in the current menu context, a four-digit zone address in a zone list, or a two-digit function number in the function editor.

navigationRules.rule: Preserve full-menu groups 20 Display, 30 Test and 50 Engineer 1. The supported subset omits other groups/options rather than renumbering them.
At the full-menu selection level, valid numeric option selection can jump to 21, 22, 31 or 52; ent enters the selected option. These are full-menu numbers, not quick-menu numbers.
Numeric selection is contextual. In a zone list, 1002 selects the address; in the function editor, 03 selects Intruder; it must not be interpreted as a global menu jump.
Common-phrase aliases belong in FINDR search/hints. Preserve the manufacturer labels in the keypad menu itself.

logViewer.fixtureNotes: All sample dates, identities and event history are fictional. Real logs may include many more event types and use group filtering.

walkTest.selectedZoneHash: Toggle inclusion; selected shows TEST and unselected shows #=TEST.
walkTest.selectedZoneEnt: Start the test after zone selection.
walkTest.triggerControl: Separate FINDR fixture button; not a Galaxy key.

functionEditor.note: Reference values preserve numeric gaps and intervening options for accurate A/B traversal. If only selected values are implemented, label that limitation and teach numeric selection instead of pretending adjacent scrolling matches the complete panel.

zoneAttributeReference.note: Group appears only when group mode is enabled. Descriptor editing has different esc/save behaviour; it is intentionally outside this bounded editor.

fixtures.hardware: Hardwired RIO practice zones; 1k double-balanced resistance examples.

zoneTrigger.note: Synthetic teaching values for the fixture only; resistance interpretation depends on installed wiring and selected resistance preset.

fixtures.note: Sample events demonstrate browsing, not real system history. Zone labels, dates, and readings are FINDR teaching fixtures.

A advances through zones; B goes back. A four-digit address also selects a zone.
The zone function and circuit status alternate on the top line.

steps.hint: Show circuit resistance and RIO voltage on the lower line.

tasks.teachingNote: The voltage belongs to the RIO. These are synthetic readings from a hardwired practice zone, not measured detector voltage.

steps.hint: B moves to an older event; A moves to a newer event.
Reveal extra details for the alarm event.
30 Test → 31 Walk Test → 2 Activate → 1 Silent → 2 Selected Zones.

Use FINDR’s separate practice trigger to simulate the detector opening and closing.
Review zones tested during this session.

limitations: Bounded practice based on a named archived edition, not a claim of current firmware or a complete Galaxy-family emulator.
The user guide documents Quick Menu shortcuts 3/4/6; this engineer trainer deliberately uses Full Menu 21/22/31. Do not combine the numbering schemes.
Only selected branches are implemented. Omitted menu options retain their real numbers if later added.
No live alarm communication, account credentials, PIN authorisation, physical output control, transmission or actual engineer logoff checks.
Menu labels and numbers are verified against the manuals. Exact screen spacing, dates, descriptors, readings and synthetic events are illustrative.
Readings apply to the fictional hardwired fixture; # displays RIO voltage, not detector voltage.
For a future authentic engineer-exit lesson, the documented action is engineer code plus esc from the engineer banner, not a numbered Log off menu option; real exit checks would also need modelling.

menu.numeric: Select the matching menu item, then Yes opens it. A numeric shortcut must not immediately enter the item.
menu.No: Context-specific change/edit key; do not globally map it to Back.
menu.Menu: Return to the preceding menu level.
menu.Scroll up: Move to the preceding available item.
menu.Scroll down: Move to the following available item.

controls.cancelCaveat: The referenced zone diagram proves No=edit and Yes=accept. It does not establish a universal discard-draft shortcut. If the app supports abandoning a draft with Menu, identify discard behaviour as a trainer rule rather than a verified firmware promise.

menus.label: Zone Setup
menus.enterBehaviour: Yes enters the first zone's type field directly. Do not insert a firmware-looking Zone Type submenu.

browseControls.Scroll up/down: Choose another zone while keeping the same field.
browseControls.No: Begin editing the displayed zone type.
browseControls.Yes: Continue to this zone's next field (Attributes 1 on the full panel).

editControls.Yes: Accept the selected type and leave edit mode; a further Yes advances to Attributes 1 in the full firmware.
editControls.No: Not a documented cancel key for this workflow.

menus.label: View Event Log
menus.choiceBehaviour: A digit opens that log directly; do not add a second confirmation.

viewerControls.Area: Toggle the second line between time/date and area information.
viewerControls.Part: Show associated programmed text where an event has it.

menus.label: Do walk test?
menus.startBehaviour: Yes opens area selection. Yes again starts the walk test for selected areas. Digits 1–8 toggle areas on the full panel.

controls.Area: Cycle normal tested-zone display, zones still needing a test, then inactivity view, then normal display.
controls.Chime: Cycle chime once, chime on each activation, no chime.

menus.inactivityView: The full menu can inspect zones not activated within a chosen number of days. Exclude or clearly label this view as unavailable if history is not simulated.
menus.testCondition: The fixture is disarmed. A simulated detector activation marks the selected zone tested.

menus.label: View Zone Status
menus.fixtureWiring: A fictional wired 2k2/4k7 loop; these readings are not universal values for every wiring configuration.

controls.Chime: Enable an activation chime for the selected zone.
controls.Omit: Temporarily disable the selected zone while this diagnostic view remains open.
controls.Menu: Leave the view; clear diagnostic omissions and chime flags for all zones.

menus.implementationRequirement: If diagnostic Omit or Chime is implemented, automatically clear it on every exit from this view, including profile switches and task resets.

controls.Yes: Complete simulated engineer logoff and show normal idle display.

fictionalFixture.description: FINDR training data; no actual installed panel is represented.
fictionalFixture.eventMembershipCaveat: The training fixture chooses membership for its small example set; it does not claim to reproduce the full panel's event filtering or mandatory-log classification.

tasks.title: Check zone resistance
tasks.goal: Select zone 002, read Secure 2k2, activate its fictional detector and observe Active 6k9.
tasks.teachingNote: Resistance appears beside the zone state. There is no separate Resistance submenu on this path.

tasks.title: Find the last alarm
tasks.goal: Find the example Zone 003 Alarm and inspect its area or zone text.
tasks.teachingNote: The first log selector uses 2 for Alarm. Inside the System log, numeric keys instead act as event-category shortcuts.

tasks.title: Walk-test a PIR
tasks.goal: Start the Area A test, activate the fictional Workshop PIR, then inspect remaining zones with Area.
tasks.teachingNote: Detector buttons beside the keypad are FINDR simulation controls, not extra panel keys.

tasks.title: Change a zone type
tasks.goal: Change fictional zone 003 from Entry/Exit 1 to Guard and accept the new value.
tasks.teachingNote: No begins editing; Yes accepts. Guard is the actual displayed type, while 'instant zone' is a FINDR search phrase.

tasks.title: Log off engineer
tasks.goal: Explicitly log off the simulated engineer session.
tasks.teachingNote: Leaving the programming display and logging off are different actions on this panel.

limitations: This is a documented subset based on named manual editions, not a complete firmware emulator or a claim about every Premier Elite revision.
The trainer starts in engineer mode and has no real PIN, default-code or authentication workflow.
No live alarm, signalling, bell, user, credential or device connection is present.
Only selected engineer options and five common zone types are supported. Unimplemented fields must be visibly marked outside the keypad display.
Aliases belong in FINDR search/help; only documented wording belongs on the simulated LCD.
A generic No=Back mapping is inaccurate here. Keep Menu and No separate.
If the UI omits the full walk-test inactivity cycle, describe the walk-test screen as a simplified practice subset.
The full manual's log events and timings are replaced by fictional fixture data. Do not imply that the sample log proves real event membership or event order.
Cancellation of an unaccepted zone-type draft is an explicit trainer rule unless separately verified; the manual only clearly establishes No to edit and Yes to accept.
Only the 24/48/88/168 walk-test branch is represented. The 640 area-group workflow is excluded.

orisec.title: Orisec CP
orisec.keypad: LCD keypad · legacy CP-25 / CP-50 / CP-100
orisec.scope: Selected test and log routes from the legacy CP-25 / CP-50 / CP-100 manual. This is a FINDR teaching simulation with fictional site data.

sources.title: CP-25 / CP-50 / CP-100 Installation Manual
sources.sourceKind: Original manufacturer manual hosted by an installer archive

controls.description: Scroll through the included menus, zones and example events.

controls.label: Enter / ▶
controls.description: Open a highlighted menu. The Back key returns a level.

controls.label: ◀ / ▶ in bell test
controls.description: Toggle the selected simulated Bell or Strobe output.

tasks.title: Check zone resistance
tasks.description: Find the simulated resistance of zone 02, HALL PIR, while the detector is active.
hints: Scroll to Tests & Diagnostics and press Enter.
Choose 03 View Zone Status, then scroll to zone 02. Its status includes the simulated resistance.

tasks.title: Find the last intruder alarm
tasks.description: Open the event log and find the example Intruder Alarm 02 entry.
hints: Scroll to System Event Logs and press Enter.
Choose View event log, then use Up / Down to find Intruder Alarm 02.

tasks.title: Walk test a detector
tasks.description: Start the test, activate demo zone 02, then stop the test with Back.
hints: Open Tests & Diagnostics, then 01 Walk Test Zones.
Use the separate demo detector button for zone 02. Press Back on the keypad to end the test.

tasks.title: Test the bell output
tasks.description: Switch the demo Bell on and back off. This exercise only changes the display; it makes no sound.
hints: Open Tests & Diagnostics, then 00 Test Bell & Strobe.
With Bell selected, use Left or Right to turn it on, then press again to turn it off.

limitations: Starts after authorisation. PIN entry, arming, signalling and connection to a real panel are outside this trainer.
Uses the legacy CP-25 / CP-50 / CP-100 manual, not every current CP model or firmware. A shared panel-family picture does not extend this scope.
Only the displayed test and event-log branches are included. Menu siblings, log filters, zone counters, reset modes and chime settings are omitted; LCD spacing and readings are illustrative.
The manual’s root-menu screenshot and shortcut text disagree. This trainer uses scrolling at that level; no root numeric shortcuts are taught.
The event names come from the manual. Names, dates, event order and zone readings belong to a fictional site. The example DEOL circuit is one detector with 2k2 EOL and 4k7 alarm resistance.
Bell and Strobe output states only change this training display. Exit practice and Reset task are FINDR controls.

integrationChecks: All menu IDs, parent/child/next links and task routeNodeIds resolve.
All task source IDs resolve within their own profile.
Every type goal starts with a different initial type.
Nineteen tasks across four profiles (Galaxy 5, Texecom 5, Scantronic 5, Orisec 4). Engine interaction tests are a separate integration gate.
